question: How many of Taiwan's 22 mayor and county magistrate seats will the KMT win in the November 28, 2026 local elections?

calls.reasoning: Reference: KMT won 15 (2018) and 14 (2022), but has no registered nominee in Hsinchu City, Chiayi City and (apparently) Chiayi County, capping it at 19. Race-by-race from Oct-Nov polls: near-safe KMT in Miaoli, Nantou, Hualien, Taoyuan; long shots in Tainan, Kaohsiung, Pingtung; genuine tossups in Taipei (polls split, Shen 'ocean wave' momentum), New Taipei, Taichung, Keelung, Hsinchu County, Changhua (KMT trails), Yilan (KMT trails), Taitung, Penghu, Kinmen, Lienchiang. Summed probabilities ~10.2; shaded down for apparent DPP momentum and thin Polymarket books (DPP 'most seats' 0.62 vs KMT 0.36; 'KMT exactly 8' 0.18 — tiny volume, near-miss contracts, used as evidence only). Correlated swing widens the spread.
sources: https://zh.wikipedia.org/zh-tw/2026年中華民國直轄市長及縣市長選舉民意調查
calls.dossier:
- Resolves off CEC count of races won by CEC-registered KMT nominees; TPP/independents endorsed by the KMT do not count. Event window: election day 2026-11-28, results due by 2027-01-05 for any postponed race. As of 2026-11-15, 13 days remain before the vote.
- KMT nominated 19 of 22 races (Focus Taiwan, Jul 2026). It stood aside in Hsinchu City (independent incumbent Ann Kao) and Chiayi City (TPP Chang Chi-kai). Wikipedia lists only DPP Tsai Yi-yu and independent Wu Pin-jui in Chiayi County.
- Historical KMT totals: 2014 6, 2018 15, 2022 14. Seats before this election per China Times (Nov 13): KMT 14, DPP 5, independents 3.
- Taipei: NTSPI (Nov 10-12) Shen (DPP) 46.3 vs Chiang (KMT incumbent) 42.2; ETtoday (Nov 1-3) Chiang 50.7 vs Shen 41.9; 信民 had Shen 50.3 vs 33.3. A scholar put Shen's win chance at ~10% if his momentum stalls, 40%+ if it continues (Storm).
- New Taipei: TRI (Nov 8-10) Lee (KMT) 43.1 vs Su (DPP) 38.4; 鋒燦 (Nov 4-10) Su 44 vs Lee 35.6; UDN (Nov 9) Su +3.
- Taoyuan: Chang (KMT incumbent) leads Huang (DPP) by 4-11 (Chi-Key Nov 4-6; ETtoday Oct 29-Nov 1).
- Taichung: Chiang (KMT) led in four of five polls since October (World News Nov 5-7: 39.2 vs 30); a DPP internal poll (Nov 8-9) has Ho (DPP) 39.9 vs 35.2.
- Kaohsiung: Lai (DPP) 40 vs Ko (KMT) 33 (UDN Oct 28-31); ETtoday Oct 20-25 roughly tied. Tainan: Chen (DPP) 59 vs 23 (Oct).
- Keelung: Hsieh (KMT incumbent) 35.1 vs Tung (DPP) 38.4 (Nov 9-11).
- Hsinchu County: Hsu (KMT) 44.4 vs Cheng (DPP) 37.5 (Chi-Key Nov 5-8).
- Changhua: Chen Su-yueh (DPP) 32, Wei (KMT) 16, Chiu (independent) 10 (UDN Oct 13-15). Outgoing KMT magistrate Wang Hui-mei campaigned for Wei on Nov 14.
- Yilan: Lin (DPP) 37.8 vs Wu (KMT) 28 (Aug — no fresher poll found).
- Nantou: Hsu (KMT incumbent) 44.6 vs Wen 30.6 (Oct). Yunlin: Chang (KMT) 49.5 vs Liu 38.9 (Mar only).
- Hualien: Yu (KMT) 30.5 vs Wei 13.6 (Nov). Taitung: Wu (KMT) 35.7 vs Chen Ying (DPP) 31.1 (Nov 6-8).
- Penghu: Chen (KMT) 28.9 vs Wu (DPP) 21.6 (Nov 2-9), seat held by the DPP. Kinmen: Chen (KMT) 45.1 vs several independents (Nov 2-5); independents beat the KMT there in 2018 and 2022. Lienchiang: KMT incumbent Wang vs independent Tsao Erh-yuan (former magistrate), no recent poll.
- Commentary: Xie Hanbing (Nov 13) says the KMT drops 1-2 seats from 14 at minimum, naming Yilan, Changhua, Chiayi and Hsinchu as at risk. Street pollster 蔡宇傑 (Jul) projected KMT 13 / DPP 8. Dai Li-an poll: 38% of respondents expect DPP ≥11 seats. Chu Li-luan warned that only ~60% of KMT supporters intend to vote.
- Many polls come from partisan-aligned outfits; there is no recent Miaoli, Chiayi County or Lienchiang polling.
- Searched for but not found: fresh Yilan, Yunlin and Changhua November polls, and Polymarket's full seat-count bracket list (page failed to load).
calls.reference_class: KMT mayor/magistrate seat totals in 2014 (6), 2018 (15) and 2022 (14) nine-in-one elections, adjusted for 19 nominated races

calls.reasoning: Reference: KMT won 15 (2018) and 14 (2022) of 22; it can win at most 20 this cycle (no nominee in Hsinchu City or Chiayi City). Per-race win probabilities from Oct-Nov 2026 polls add up to ~10.5. Safe KMT: Miaoli, Nantou, Taitung, Lienchiang, Kinmen (Chen Yu-chen 45% vs 15%). Leaning KMT: Taoyuan, Yunlin, Hualien (three-way, Yu leads), Penghu (six-way after DPP incumbent withdrew). Toss-ups with conflicting polls: Taipei, New Taipei, Taichung, Keelung, Hsinchu County. Leaning DPP: Yilan, Changhua (Chen Su-yue 32% vs Wei 16%). Safe DPP: Tainan, Kaohsiung, Pingtung, Chiayi County. Median nudged up to 11 because polls understated the KMT in 2022 and pundits project 12-13. No matching market: Polymarket's two 'KMT wins most' contracts disagree (~71% on the party-winner event vs 0.36 on a thin 'mayoral' variant); 'KMT wins 8' is at 0.18 on ~$331 volume; these are evidence, not anchors.
sources: https://zh.wikipedia.org/zh-tw/2026年中華民國直轄市長及縣市長選舉民意調查
calls.dossier:
- Structure: 22 races. The KMT is not running in Hsinchu City or Chiayi City (backing the TPP), so its maximum is 20. Background: KMT won 15 in 2018 and 14 in 2022; in 2022 Miaoli and Kinmen went to independents, Hsinchu City to the TPP, Penghu to the DPP. Fine print: only CEC-registered KMT candidates count.
- Resolves off the CEC (db.cec.gov.tw) results of the 2026-11-28 election, not off polls or endorsements. Event window: election 2026-11-28; postponed races count if decided by 2027-01-05. As of 2026-11-15 the vote is 13 days away.
- Taipei (KMT incumbent Chiang Wan-an vs DPP Puma Shen): New Taiwan Strategy Nov 10-12, Shen 46.3 vs Chiang 42.2; Taiwan Strategy Research Assoc. (Nov 2), Shen 52.6-35.3; TPOC AI simulation, Chiang 45.9-43.1.
- New Taipei (KMT Lee Shu-chuan vs DPP Su Chiao-hui): UDN Nov 9, Su 42-39; Taiwan Research Assoc. Nov 8-10, Lee 43.1-38.4.
- Taoyuan (KMT incumbent Chang San-cheng): 36.9 vs 32.8 (Nov 4-6). Joint KMT-TPP rally Nov 14; Eric Chu warned that only ~60% of KMT supporters intend to vote.
- Taichung (KMT Johnny Chiang vs DPP Ho Hsin-chun): Fo Guang Univ., Chiang 38.3-28.1; DPP internal poll Nov 8-9, Ho 39.9-35.2.
- Tainan: DPP 59.4 vs KMT 22.6 (Oct). Kaohsiung: UDN Oct 28-31, DPP Lai 40 vs KMT Ko 33. Pingtung and Chiayi County are DPP strongholds.
- Keelung (KMT incumbent Hsieh Kuo-liang): Thinking Media Nov 9-11, DPP Tung 38.4 vs Hsieh 35.1.
- Hsinchu County (KMT-TPP cooperation collapsed): ERA Nov 8-10, DPP Cheng 36.9 vs KMT Hsu 28.6; Taiwan Public Policy Research Assoc. Nov 5-8, Hsu 44.4-37.5.
- Changhua (open seat, three/four-way race): UDN Oct 13-15, DPP Chen Su-yue 32 vs KMT Wei 16, 42% undecided. Yilan: an FTV pundit poll had DPP Lin Kuo-chang at 53% over KMT Wu Tsung-hsien; the former KMT magistrate there was convicted.
- Lean/safe KMT: Miaoli (Chung Tung-chin, now KMT-registered, ~58-42), Yunlin (Chang Chia-chun ~55-45), Nantou (Hsu Shu-hua >50%), Taitung (KMT Wu 55 vs 24/21), Kinmen (KMT Chen Yu-chen 45.1 vs 14.8, seven-way race), Lienchiang.
- Hualien, three-way (KMT Yu Shu-chen vs independents Chang Chun and Wei Chia-hsien): Storm Media, Yu 30.5 / 19.1 / 13.6; another poll Yu 28.5 vs Chang 25.7.
- Penghu, six-way: the DPP incumbent withdrew for health reasons and his wife is running; ETtoday Aug, KMT Chen Chen-chung 30.3 vs Wu Shu-chin ~21; an independent former Magong mayor is also running.
- Pundits (China Times, Nov 13): KMT may drop 1-2 from 14; Yilan, Changhua, Chiayi and Hsinchu flagged as at risk. Street pollster Tsai Yu-chieh: KMT 13 / DPP 8 / independent 1. TPOC Sept: KMT ahead in 14 races.
- Searched but not found: a reliable recent poll for Pingtung, Chiayi County or Lienchiang, and a liquid market on the exact KMT seat count.
calls.reference_class: KMT executive-seat totals in Taiwan's 2014/2018/2022 local elections (6, 15, 14 of 22), combined with per-race polling in 2026

calls.reasoning: The KMT has official nominees in only 19 races (it stood aside in Hsinchu City and Chiayi City, and has none in Chiayi County), so 19 is the ceiling. The base rate is the 14-15 seats it won in 2018 and 2022 and the 14 races it led in TPOC's September model. Late polls show safe or strong KMT seats in Taipei, Taoyuan, Miaoli, Nantou, Kinmen, Lienchiang, Taichung and Yunlin; KMT leads in New Taipei, Hsinchu County, Taitung and Penghu; a Keelung incumbent now trailing (35.1-38.4); a three-way tie in Hualien; and DPP leads in Changhua (32-16), Yilan, Tainan, Kaohsiung and Pingtung. Per-race probabilities sum to about 11. Pundits say 13-14. On markets, no Polymarket contract matches; the near-miss 'KMT wins Taipei and New Taipei' at 0.36 suggests New Taipei is closer to a coin flip than the polls imply. A correlated national swing widens the distribution.

calls.dossier:
- Election is Nov 28, 2026. Event window: the CEC count on election night, with postponed races counted if known by Jan 5, 2027; as of Nov 15, 2026 the vote has not happened. Resolves off official KMT nominees registered with the CEC; TPP and independent winners do not count.
- KMT nominees exist in 19 races. There is no KMT nominee in Hsinchu City (independent Kao Hung-an is the incumbent), Chiayi City (TPP's Chang Chi-kai) or Chiayi County (DPP's Tsai Yi-yu vs independent Wu Pin-jui). Ceiling: 19. (Wikipedia, 2026 Taiwanese local elections)
- Past KMT seat totals: 2014: 6, 2018: 15, 2022: 14 of 22. KMT held 14 seats going in.
- TPOC model (Sep 8, 2026): KMT led in 14 races (Keelung, Taipei, New Taipei, Taoyuan, Hsinchu County, Miaoli, Taichung, Nantou, Yunlin, Hualien, Taitung, Penghu, Kinmen, Lienchiang); DPP led in 7 (Yilan, Changhua, Chiayi County, Chiayi City, Tainan, Kaohsiung, Pingtung). New Taipei was later unified behind KMT nominee Lee Shu-chuan.
- New Taipei: Lee (KMT) 43.1 vs Su Chiao-hui (DPP) 38.4 (Nov 8-10 poll). Chinatimes (Nov 13) says polls there trade leads.
- Taipei: Chiang Wan-an (KMT incumbent) leads in all polls but by modest margins (Chinatimes, Nov 13).
- Taichung: Johnny Chiang (KMT) 39.2 vs Ho Hsin-chun (DPP) 30 (Nov 5-7).
- Keelung: DPP's Tung 38.4 vs incumbent Hsieh (KMT) 35.1 (Nov 9-11); among certain voters 48.5 vs 39.5. An earlier poll had Hsieh 36.1 vs Tung 35.6.
- Hualien: KMT's Yu Shu-chen 25.3, independent Wei Chia-hsien 25.1, independent Chang Chun about 25 (Nov 11-12).
- Changhua: DPP's Chen Su-yueh 32 vs KMT's Wei Ping-cheng 16, independent Chiu Chien-fu 10, 42% undecided (UDN, mid-Oct). A Nov 12 street poll also had Chen ahead.
- Yilan: DPP's Lin Kuo-chang 37.8 vs KMT's Wu Tsung-hsien 28 (Aug 26-29; nothing newer found). Commentator flags Yilan, Changhua and Chiayi as KMT danger areas and Hsinchu as risky.
- Hsinchu County: KMT's Hsu Hsin-ying 44.4 vs DPP's Cheng 37.5 (Nov 5-8). The TPP ended its partnership with the KMT in Hsinchu County in Sep.
- Taitung: KMT's Wu Hsiu-hua 35.7 vs DPP's Chen Ying 31.1 (Nov 6-8). Penghu: KMT 28.9 vs DPP 21.6 (Nov 2-9). Kinmen: KMT 45.1 vs independent 14.8. Yunlin: KMT 49.5 vs DPP 38.9 (March, old).
- Pingtung (DPP incumbent), Tainan and Kaohsiung are long-standing DPP strongholds.
- Pundit predictions range from 13 KMT seats (street-poll host, July) to 16 (blog); one commentator says the KMT will lose 1-2 seats from 14.
- Turnout worry: Eric Chu (Nov 14) said only about 60% of KMT supporters intend to vote.
- Searched for but not found: recent Yilan, Yunlin, Miaoli or Nantou polls, and any market matching this exact seat-count contract.
calls.reference_class: KMT seat counts among the 22 executive races in Taiwan's 2014, 2018 and 2022 local elections (6, 15, 14), adjusted to the 19 races with a KMT nominee

calls.reasoning: KMT holds 14 seats and won 15 (2018) and 14 (2022), but this cycle's ceiling is 19 (no nominee in Hsinchu City, Chiayi City, Chiayi County). Race-by-race from Oct-Nov polls: strong KMT in Taoyuan, Miaoli, Nantou, Yunlin; lean KMT in Taipei, Taichung, Hsinchu County, Taitung, Kinmen, Lienchiang; toss-ups in New Taipei, Hualien, Penghu, Keelung; lean DPP in Yilan and Changhua; near-safe DPP in Tainan, Kaohsiung, Pingtung. Per-race sum ~10.2, nudged up slightly because polls historically understated the KMT, offset by soft KMT turnout and DPP momentum. Thin Polymarket near-miss contracts (DPP most seats 0.62) fit a median near 10.
calls.reconciliation: Factual: Chiayi County nominee (runs 1 and 3 say none, run 2 says safe DPP) changes about 0 expected seats, so it doesn't need settling. Ceiling taken as 19. The remaining disputes are judgment: Taipei (conflicting polls, partisan-aligned sources; I gave Chiang ~0.65), and whether to shade for the KMT's past poll outperformance (runs 2 and 3) or for DPP momentum and thin markets (run 1). No new evidence settles these. I take the per-race sum ~10.2 plus a small upward nudge, giving a median of 10.5, between runs 1 and 2/3 on the evidence rather than by averaging. Kept the runs' dispersion of ~5. No market matches the contract; Polymarket near-misses used as evidence only.
